title: Rounding Decimals
kicker: Cambridge Primary Checkpoint · Mathematics 0096 · Stage 6 · Number
summary: Round numbers with two decimal places to the nearest tenth or whole number, work backwards from a rounded value, and use rounding to estimate — with number lines, worked examples and a Checkpoint-style quiz.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Round numbers with 2 decimal places to the nearest tenth or to the nearest whole number (6Np.04)

blocks.text: Rounding gives a simpler number that is **close** to the real one. We round to make estimates, to check answers, and to give sensible measurements ("the plank is about 1.7 m long"). In Stage 6 you round numbers with **two decimal places**, like 3.47, either to the **nearest whole number** or to the **nearest tenth** (one decimal place).
Key words

items: round
يقرّب — replace a number with a simpler number that is close to it
nearest whole number
لأقرب عدد صحيح — the answer has no decimal places: 6.38 → 6
nearest tenth
لأقرب جزء من عشرة — the answer has one decimal place: 3.47 → 3.5
decimal place (d.p.)
منزلة عشرية — a place after the point; 3.47 has 2 decimal places
deciding digit
الرقم اللي بيحدد — the digit just to the right of the place you are rounding to
halfway
المنتصف — exactly in the middle of the two choices, e.g. 3.45 between 3.4 and 3.5
estimate
تقدير — a quick, rough answer found with rounded numbers
"is approximately equal to" — يساوي تقريبًا: 4.82 + 3.19 ≈ 8

blocks.text: 1. Rounding on a number line
To round, ask: **which of the two possible answers is the number closer to?** A number line makes this easy to see.

blocks.text: 2. Rounding to the nearest whole number

items: Find the two whole numbers the number lies between (6.38 lies between 6 and 7).
Look at the **tenths digit** only — this is the deciding digit.
If the tenths digit is **0, 1, 2, 3 or 4**, round **down**: keep the ones digit (6.38 → 6).
If the tenths digit is **5, 6, 7, 8 or 9**, round **up**: add 1 to the ones digit (6.51 → 7).
Write the answer with **no** decimal places.

blocks.text: Notice 12.49 rounds **down** to 12. It is very close to 12.5, but it is still less than halfway. Only the tenths digit (4) matters — the hundredths digit (9) does not change the answer.
3. Rounding to the nearest tenth

items: Find the two tenths the number lies between (3.47 lies between 3.4 and 3.5).
Look at the **hundredths digit** — this is the deciding digit.
0–4: round **down** (keep the tenths digit). 5–9: round **up** (add 1 to the tenths digit).
Write the answer with **exactly one** decimal place — even if that digit is 0.

blocks.text: **Rounding up past a 9.** 4.96 lies between 4.9 and 5.0. Adding 1 tenth to 4.9 gives 5.0. Write **5.0**, not 4.10 and not 5. The ".0" shows that you rounded to the nearest tenth.
4. Two important rules
**Halfway rounds up.** A number exactly halfway, like 7.45 (between 7.4 and 7.5) or 6.50 (between 6 and 7), is rounded **up**: 7.45 → 7.5 and 6.50 → 7.

**Round only once, from the original number.** To round 2.47 to the nearest whole number, look at the tenths digit (4) straight away: 2.47 → 2. Do **not** round to 2.5 first and then to 3. 2.47 is less than 2.5, so it is closer to 2.
5. Working backwards: which numbers round to …?
Checkpoint often turns the question round: "A number with 2 decimal places rounds to 4.3. What is the smallest/largest it could be?"

items: Find the halfway points either side of 4.3: halfway between 4.2 and 4.3 is **4.25**; halfway between 4.3 and 4.4 is **4.35**.
Halfway rounds up, so 4.25 rounds to 4.3 (allowed) but 4.35 rounds to 4.4 (not allowed).
So the 2-decimal-place numbers that round to 4.3 go from **4.25** (smallest) to **4.34** (largest).

blocks.text: 6. Using rounding to estimate
Round each number to the nearest whole number, then calculate. The estimate helps you check an exact answer.

items: 4.82 + 3.19 ≈ 5 + 3 = 8 (exact answer 8.01 — close, so it looks right).
A book costs $3.95. Four books cost about 4 × 4 = $16 (exact $15.80).

blocks.title: إزاي تقرّب؟
items: لأقرب عدد صحيح: بص على رقم الأجزاء من عشرة (أول رقم بعد العلامة). لأقرب جزء من عشرة: بص على رقم الأجزاء من مئة (تاني رقم بعد العلامة).
لو الرقم ٠ أو ١ أو ٢ أو ٣ أو ٤ → سيب الرقم زي ما هو. لو ٥ أو أكتر → زوّد واحد.
قرّب مرة واحدة بس من الرقم الأصلي: ٢٫٤٧ لأقرب عدد صحيح = ٢ مش ٣.
٤٫٩٦ لأقرب جزء من عشرة = ٥٫٠ — اكتب الصفر!

blocks.text: Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — Round 14.63 (a) to the nearest whole number (b) to the nearest tenth. [2 marks]

items: (a) The tenths digit is 6 (5 or more), so round up: 14 → **15**.
(b) The hundredths digit is 3 (less than 5), so round down: **14.6**.

blocks.text: **Common mistake:** giving 14.6 for part (a). Read the question carefully: "whole number" means no decimal places.
**Worked example 2** — Round 8.97 to the nearest tenth. [1 mark]

8.97 lies between 8.9 and 9.0. The hundredths digit is 7, so round up: 8.9 + 0.1 = 9.0. **Answer: 9.0.** **Common mistake:** writing 8.10 ("9 + 1 = 10") — the tenths cannot hold 10, so you carry into the ones.
**Worked example 3** — Ring all the numbers that round to 3 to the nearest whole number: 2.49  2.50  3.48  3.51  2.81 [1 mark]

items: 2.49 → tenths digit 4 → rounds to 2 ✗
2.50 → tenths digit 5 → rounds up to 3 ✓
3.48 → tenths digit 4 → stays 3 ✓
3.51 → tenths digit 5 → rounds up to 4 ✗
2.81 → tenths digit 8 → rounds up to 3 ✓

blocks.text: **Answer:** ring 2.50, 3.48 and 2.81. All three must be ringed (and no others) for the mark.
**Worked example 4** — A number has 2 decimal places. Rounded to the nearest tenth it is 5.7. Write the smallest and the largest number it could be. [2 marks]

Halfway between 5.6 and 5.7 is 5.65, which rounds up to 5.7 ✓. Halfway between 5.7 and 5.8 is 5.75, which rounds up to 5.8 ✗, so the largest is one hundredth less: 5.74. **Answer:** smallest 5.65, largest 5.74. **Common mistake:** giving 5.75 as the largest.
**Worked example 5** — Mona buys 2.85 kg of potatoes, 1.32 kg of onions and 0.94 kg of tomatoes. Estimate the total mass by rounding each mass to the nearest whole number. [1 mark]
2.85 → 3, 1.32 → 1, 0.94 → 1. Estimate: 3 + 1 + 1 = **5 kg**. (The exact total is 5.11 kg, so the estimate is good.) Show the rounded numbers — that is the method the question is testing.
**Worked example 6** — Omar says: "6.45 rounded to the nearest whole number is 7, because 5 rounds up." Explain why Omar is wrong. [1 mark]

**Answer:** To round to the nearest whole number you look at the tenths digit, which is 4, so 6.45 rounds down to 6. (6.45 is less than 6.5, the halfway point.) Omar looked at the hundredths digit, which is only used when rounding to the nearest tenth.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Looking at the wrong digit. Whole number → look at tenths. Nearest tenth → look at hundredths.
Rounding twice: 2.47 → 2.5 → 3 is wrong; 2.47 → 2 is right.
Dropping the zero: 4.96 to the nearest tenth is 5.0, not 5.
Writing 8.10 for 8.97 rounded to one decimal place. Carry into the ones: 9.0.
Changing the digits you keep when rounding down: 3.42 → 3.4, not 3.3.
Giving 4.35 as the largest number that rounds to 4.3 — it rounds to 4.4.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: "Round 6.38 to the nearest whole number" / "to the nearest tenth" — answer in a box.
"Ring the numbers that round to …" or "Tick the correct answer" — check every number, one by one.
Complete a table: one column "nearest whole number", another "nearest tenth".
Number lines: a point on a scale going up in hundredths, then "round it to the nearest tenth".
Reverse questions: smallest/largest number, or use digit cards to make a number that rounds to a given value.
Estimation: "Estimate … by rounding each number to the nearest whole number. Show your working." Write the rounded numbers.
"Explain" questions: name the deciding digit and say whether it is less than 5 or 5 or more.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Rounding decimals — practice
blocks.intro: 14 questions, from easy to Checkpoint-hard. No calculator. Type numbers only. For the explain question, write your answer and mark it with the mark scheme.

questions.e: The hundredths digit is 7 (5 or more), so round up: 5.3 → 5.4.

questions.q: Round 12.82 to the nearest whole number.
questions.e: The tenths digit is 8 (5 or more), so round up: 12 → 13.

questions.q: Round 0.49 to the nearest whole number.
questions.e: The tenths digit is 4 (less than 5), so round down to 0. 0.49 is less than halfway (0.5) between 0 and 1.
7.45 is exactly halfway between 7.4 and 7.5. The hundredths digit is 5, so round up: 7.5.

questions.q: What is 3.96 rounded to the nearest tenth?
questions.e: The hundredths digit is 6, so round up: 3.9 + 0.1 = 4.0. (3.10 is a common mistake: the 9 tenths become 10 tenths = 1 whole.)

questions.q: Which number rounds to 6 to the nearest whole number?
A ribbon is 1.65 m long. What is its length to the nearest tenth of a metre?
questions.e: 1.65 is halfway between 1.6 and 1.7. Halfway rounds up, so 1.7 m.

questions.e: Each small interval is 0.01, so the arrow shows 2.46. The hundredths digit is 6, so round up: 2.5. (2.46 is the number itself, not the rounded value.)
9.95 is halfway between 9.9 and 10.0, so round up: 9.9 + 0.1 = 10.0. On paper write 10.0 to show one decimal place (type 10 or 10.0 here).

questions.p: A number has 2 decimal places. When it is rounded to the nearest tenth, the answer is 8.3.
questions.q: (a) What is the smallest the number could be?
questions.e: Halfway between 8.2 and 8.3 is 8.25, and halfway rounds up to 8.3. So the smallest is 8.25.

questions.p: A number has 2 decimal places. When it is rounded to the nearest tenth, the answer is 8.3.
questions.q: (b) What is the largest the number could be?
questions.e: 8.35 would round up to 8.4, so the largest 2-decimal-place number is one hundredth less: 8.34.

questions.q: Estimate 4.82 + 3.19 by rounding each number to the nearest whole number first.
Use each of the digit cards 2, 4 and 8 once to make a number ☐.☐☐ that rounds to 4.3 to the nearest tenth.
questions.e: To round to 4.3 the ones digit must be 4, so the cards 2 and 8 go after the point: 4.28 or 4.82. 4.28 → hundredths digit 8 → rounds up to 4.3 ✓. 4.82 → 4.8 ✗. Answer 4.28. (1 mark for a number with 4 in the ones place, e.g. 4.82.)

questions.q: Rania rounds 2.47 to the nearest whole number. She writes: "2.47 → 2.5 → 3". Explain her mistake and write the correct answer.
questions.ms: 1 mark: explanation, e.g. she rounded twice / she should round only once from 2.47 / to the nearest whole number you look at the tenths digit (4), which is less than 5 / 2.47 is less than 2.5 (halfway), so it is closer to 2. 1 mark: correct answer 2. Do not accept 'she should have rounded down' with no reason for the explanation mark.
questions.e: Rania rounded twice. For the nearest whole number, look only at the tenths digit of the original number: it is 4, so 2.47 rounds down to 2. 2.47 is less than 2.5, so it is closer to 2 than to 3.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Nearest whole number → look at the tenths digit. Nearest tenth → look at the hundredths digit.
0–4 round down (keep the digit); 5–9 round up (add 1). Exactly halfway rounds up.
Round once, from the original number: 2.47 → 2, never 2.47 → 2.5 → 3.
Keep one decimal place when rounding to the nearest tenth, even if it is 0: 4.96 → 5.0.
Numbers that round to 4.3 (nearest tenth) go from 4.25 to 4.34.
